title: a-watchme-names-its-receiver
intention: A WATCHME spec names its receiver — what receives the probe's data and in which component — and a spec without one is refused at cast, at the crossing, and flagged by the at-rest ticket inspection.
why: Akien, 2026-10-01: 'I think we've just been doing 1' — probes were built and nothing receives what they send. Measured: 138 of 138 WATCHME specs name a person in prose as consumer and none names code that receives. The lived symptom: probes fire into the void, and the efficacy question a WATCHME was carried for is never answered by anything that acts on it.
traces_to: Akien's ruling, item 2 of ~/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md (2026-10-01). Memory a-probe-needs-a-consumer (RULED 2026-09-30): no consumer that USES the data = trash; receiver first. Law 1: watchme_present in cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/inspector.py is a second opinion of watchme_spec.REQUIRED_FIELDS and already disagrees (it checks 5 fields; the spec requires 7). Measured 2026-10-01: 138 of 138 WATCHME specs carry 'consumer', a prose field naming a person or role (e.g. 'CodeMother, who owns the care of the code'); 0 carry a receiver naming code in a component.
how: In cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py add RECEIVER_FIELD = 'receiver': a dict {'what': non-empty str naming the code that receives, 'in': repo-relative component directory}; watchme_spec_error faults a spec whose receiver is absent, not a dict, has an empty 'what', or whose 'in' is not a directory holding intention+why.json, naming every fault in one message. cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/inspector.py's watchme_present check stops spelling its own field list and reports watchme_spec_error's text, so there is one opinion about a complete spec. The sweep tooth in cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_watchme_spec.py changes from 'no fault' to 'no fault except a missing receiver', and records the measured list of specs lacking one as the work list of the receiver-backfill ticket.
falsifier: RED if: (1) a spec complete in every current field but with no receiver passes watchme_spec_error; (2) a receiver whose 'in' is not a directory holding intention+why.json passes; (3) a receiver with an empty 'what' passes; (4) a spec with a valid receiver is refused; (5) the ticket inspector's watchme_present finding on a receiver-less fixture does not carry watchme_spec_error's text; (6) the real corpus sweep shows any fault other than a missing receiver. Horizon: the tester seal.
watchme: none, because the receiver of this rule is the cast door and the crossing gate in cairn/tools/base/transitions.py, which call watchme_spec_error on every ticket that carries a watch
children: none, because the receiver backfill over the 138 standing specs is its own sibling ticket cast after this one is PROVED, with its work list measured by this ticket's sweep tooth in cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_watchme_spec.py
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) The shape? receiver = {'what': str, 'in': 'cairn/devices/codemother'}; 'in' resolved against the repo root and must contain intention+why.json. (2) Where does the fault text go? appended to the same faults list in watchme_spec_error as the REQUIRED_FIELDS faults, e.g. "WATCHME(obj) spec names no receiver — a probe with nothing that USES its data is trash (Akien, 2026-10-01)". (3) The inspector? for a ticket whose state carries WATCHME, err = watchme_spec_error(t); if err: finding('watchme_present', err).

chart_claim.filled_by: CC chart chain (orient 07d22a2721f1 .. validate 2bde01e3e9f6, each learned)

decisions.text: STEP 1, the red teeth, measured 2026-10-01. (a) In cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_watchme_spec.py: the _spec helper (line 51) gains a default 'receiver': {'what': 'the owner reads the verdict', 'in': 'cairn/tools/base'} so every existing fixture stays a complete spec. Add four teeth above the TESTS list and append them to it (the file runs as a script over TESTS, printing ok/FAIL): test_a_spec_without_a_receiver_is_refused (_spec(obj) with receiver popped, inside {'workflow_and_state': _V2_WATCH, 'watchme': spec}: watchme_spec_error returns text containing 'receiver'); test_a_receiver_outside_a_component_is_refused (receiver in='cairn/no_such_component': text contains 'receiver'); test_a_receiver_naming_nothing_is_refused (receiver what='': text contains 'receiver'); test_a_valid_receiver_passes (the default _spec: watchme_spec_error is None). (b) Narrow test_the_real_ticket_corpus_is_not_retro_redded (line 154): red = rows whose error, split on '; ', has any part not containing 'names no receiver' — so a missing receiver is allowed and every other fault still reds; the backfill ticket's work list is re-derived by running python3 cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py, whose __main__ already prints every red row, so nothing is written to a file. (c) In cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/proofs/test_inspector.py: test_watchme_with_spec_is_clean (line 143) adds receiver={'what': 'w', 'in': 'cairn/tools/base'} to its spec; add test_watchme_present_carries_the_spec_rule_text: CLEAN_TICKET with the same WATCHME(x) workflow and that spec minus receiver; the watchme_present finding's 'finding' text equals watchme_spec_error of the ticket (import watchme_spec_error from cairn.tools.base.watchme_spec inside the tooth). That file runs through print_teeth_main(__file__), which discovers test_* functions, so no list to register in. (d) Add PROVES = {'fa4a411c96be': {'1': 'test_a_spec_without_a_receiver_is_refused', '2': 'test_a_receiver_outside_a_component_is_refused', '3': 'test_a_receiver_naming_nothing_is_refused', '4': 'test_a_valid_receiver_passes', '6': 'test_the_real_ticket_corpus_is_not_retro_redded'}} to test_watchme_spec.py and PROVES = {'fa4a411c96be': {'5': 'test_watchme_present_carries_the_spec_rule_text'}} to test_inspector.py. Run both red: (a)'s three refusal teeth and (c)'s text tooth fail; the valid tooth and the sweep pass before the build, which is expected.

STEP 2, the build. In cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py, beside BERTH_FIELD: RECEIVER_FIELD = 'receiver'. In watchme_spec_error, in the per-object loop after the berth check: rec = spec.get(RECEIVER_FIELD); if not a dict -> fault 'WATCHME(%s) spec names no receiver — a probe with nothing that USES its data is trash (Akien, 2026-10-01); give receiver: {"what": <the code that receives>, "in": <component dir>}'; else if rec.get('what') is not a non-empty str -> fault 'WATCHME(%s) receiver names no what'; else if 'in' is not a non-empty str or not (_REPO_ROOT / rec['in'] / 'intention+why.json').is_file() -> fault 'WATCHME(%s) receiver in=%r is not a component (no intention+why.json there)'. All three contain the word receiver; only the first contains 'names no receiver', which is the one fault the narrowed sweep allows. In cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/inspector.py replace the whole 'if "WATCHME" in state:' block's dict/list field loops with: from cairn.tools.base.watchme_spec import watchme_spec_error (module-level import beside the others); err = watchme_spec_error(t); if err: finding('watchme_present', err, {}). Keep the 'no watchme field' finding text only as what watchme_spec_error already says (it reports a carried WATCHME with no spec). Run both proofs green twice.

STEP 3, the other readers, measured 2026-10-01 by grep for '"nexus"' in proofs: cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_emission_gate.py (same component — its fixtures gain a receiver in this build), and in OTHER components skills/sorted/proofs/test_sorted_door.py, cairn/machines/skill_block/proofs/test_skill_block.py, cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_first_rider.py, cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict/proofs/test_chart_verdict.py. After the build run all five. Any of the four other-component proofs that reds only because its fixture spec lacks a receiver is NOT edited here (RULE 1): it is cast as its own ticket at that component before this ticket crosses PROVEME, and the red is named in this ticket's PROVEME note. skills/sorted/door.py line 153 spells its own missing-field list for its message; it still refuses through watchme_spec_error at line 144, so its message under-reports and that is the same other-component ticket.

D1 measured 2026-10-01: in cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_watchme_spec.py, _spec(obj, **over) at line 51 builds a dict with keys object, trigger, enough, carrier, nexus, consumer, probe, then s.update(over) and returns s. Add one key to that literal: "receiver": {"what": "the owner reads the verdict", "in": "cairn/tools/base"} — every existing caller gets a complete spec, and a tooth that needs it missing calls s = _spec(obj); s.pop('receiver'), or overrides it with receiver={...}. TESTS is the plain list at line 214 (TESTS = [ ... ] ending at line 229); define the four new teeth as module-level functions above it and append their names as the last four entries. Each tooth is a plain assert, the same shape as test_a_spec_with_no_berth_cannot_be_gated: err = ws.watchme_spec_error({'workflow_and_state': _V2_WATCH, 'watchme': spec}); assert err and 'receiver' in err, err (or assert err is None for the valid one). The object passed to _spec is 'does-the-emission-gate-fire-in-anger', the WATCHME carried by _V2_WATCH.

D3's method, deterministic: after D2 is built, run each of the five proofs with python3 <path>. A proof that was green at HEAD before the build (run it once before building and keep the output) and reds after it is caused by this build, whatever its text says — this build changed nothing else. If that proof is in cairn/tools/base (test_emission_gate.py), fix its fixture spec in this build by adding receiver={'what': ..., 'in': 'cairn/tools/base'}; if it is in another component, cast it as its own ticket (mkticket via /intent and /sorted, owning intention this ticket) naming the failing tooth and the output line, and name that ticket id in this ticket's PROVEME note. A proof red at HEAD before the build is not this build's red and is left as it stood.
